2608.19670.title: The Asymmetric Harms of LLM Compression
2608.19670.paper_summary: Large language models (LLMs) compression reduces deployment costs, but standard aggregate metrics like perplexity and accuracy often mask underlying behavioral shifts. In this work, we systematically evaluate 3 LLMs across 11 compression methods to investigate the effects of compression on knowledge retention, model confidence, and social bias. We find that compression disproportionately reduces the relative retention of head knowledge compared to tail knowledge. Furthermore, compressed models often remain substantially confident in their incorrect answers on newly lost knowledge. Finally, we demonstrate that stable aggregate bias scores can conceal substantial, opposing shifts in stereotypical preferences across demographic subgroups. Together, these findings reveal asymmetric behavioral changes that aggregate performance measures fail to capture, highlighting the need for granular evaluation of compressed models before deployment.
2608.19670.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）的壓縮降低了部署成本，但像困惑度和準確度這樣的標準綜合指標往往掩蓋了潛在的行為變化。<lb/>在這項工作中，我們系統地評估了3個LLM在11種壓縮方法下的表現，以調查壓縮對知識保留、模型信心和社會偏見的影響。<lb/>我們發現，壓縮不成比例地減少了頭部知識相對於尾部知識的保留。<lb/>此外，壓縮模型通常對其在新丟失知識上的錯誤答案仍然保持相當的信心。<lb/>最後，我們展示了穩定的綜合偏見分數可能掩蓋了不同人口子群中刻板印象偏好方面的重大對立變化。<lb/>這些發現共同揭示了綜合性能指標未能捕捉的不對稱行為變化，突顯了在部署前對壓縮模型進行細緻評估的必要性。
